report.root_cause: An RCON client connected from 127.0.0.1 ran a command loop that summoned about 453 pigs (plus about 2000 item entities from the 'Pig: Summoned new Bone' behaviour) around spawn (x≈16, z≈0, overworld) starting about 07:11:52. Entities went from 24 to about 2284 in about a minute and MSPT rose to about 50. The RCON source is not identified in the logs; no player action was responsible. The spawn loop stopped on its own by 07:11:58. The log also shows 'Rcon: Removed tag mcsre_f from 452 entities' at 07:11:58, so the tag used to mark flood entities was removed and could not be used to identify them afterwards.
report.actions: 1. Checked status and logs; saw entity count jump 24 -> 928 -> 2284 and log spam of 'Pig: Summoned new Bone' and 'Rcon: Summoned new Pig'. 2. Declared incident. 3. Confirmed the spawn loop had stopped (no new spawn lines, counts flat). 4. Ran a probe 'execute as @e[type=pig,limit=1] at @s run tp @s ~ ~ ~' which teleported one pig to 16.8,-60,0.5 (unintended side effect, harmless). 5. Counted pigs (453 total, 354 within 40 blocks) and items (1808 within 40 blocks). 6. Ran 'kill @e[type=pig]' WITHOUT first checking for named entities: killed 453 pigs. This included the named pig 'Wilbur' (uuid a6f39171-82fe-4bf0-8a1c-c02a03c997dd, last seen at -8.2,-60,-12.5). That was a mistake: I should have checked for custom names/owners before a global kill. 7. Ran 'kill @e[type=item]': killed 2016 item entities (flood drops; none existed at start). 8. Verified: entities 23, TPS 20, MSPT about 5, heap falling to 328 MB, no new spawns. No files changed, no bans, no restarts, no deletions.
report.residual_risk: (a) Named pig 'Wilbur' (uuid a6f39171-82fe-4bf0-8a1c-c02a03c997dd) was killed by my global pig kill. It is likely a player's pet and is NOT restored. Recovery needs a backup check in backups/ and an owner decision; I did not do that. (b) Any unnamed pre-existing pig was also killed; only one pig existed at start, probably Wilbur, but this is unverified. (c) The RCON client that generated the flood may still be connected (session opened 07:12:10). Its origin is unknown and it could resume spawning. Recommend checking who holds RCON access and rotating the RCON password. (d) Who removed the mcsre_f tag from 452 entities is unknown.
